_note: Exact ai-cli arguments for round 4 (ai decide -m <model> --input text, post text on stdin). Questions within a group are asked in one call. stance, believes, dismisses, topic, position and reason are verbatim from round 3; on_topic, policy_politics and frame are new in round 4. The same groups and wording are used for all three models in the model comparison.

args: stance=What is the author's stance on whether AI could be conscious? reject = dismisses it; curious = unsure, open or just interested; serious = treats it as a real possibility or deserving moral concern
believes=Does the author think current AI might be conscious or deserve moral consideration?
dismisses=Does the author treat AI consciousness or model welfare as a joke, delusion, or psychosis?
on_topic=Is this post about whether machines or AI systems can be conscious, have minds, or deserve moral consideration?
policy_politics=Does this post argue about policy or politics (company rules, regulation, who controls AI, culture-war camps) rather than about whether machines have minds?

frame=How is the post framed? political_cultural = as a political, cultural or tribal fight (for example calling AI-welfare views a religion or cult, or attacking a company or camp); philosophical_scientific = as a philosophical or scientific question about minds, consciousness or evidence; neither = no clear framing or off-topic

position=What is the author's position on Anthropic's usage-policy rule banning sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior toward Claude? support = approves of the rule; oppose = disapproves or mocks it; neutral_or_unclear = just reports it, or no clear position

reason=What is the author's main reason? oppose_absurd = it is absurd to protect software; oppose_overreach = a company should not police how paying users behave; support_model_welfare = Claude might be harmed or might matter morally; support_user_character = cruelty harms the user or society; other = none of these or no reason given
topic=Is this post arguing about the policy itself (rules, enforcement, company control of users, how people should treat chatbots) rather than about whether AI is conscious?
policy._note: Asked only for posts in the anthropic_abuse_policy flashpoint and the 20 policy hand labels.
